about: Which <send target> values name a Mesh peer, written out by hand.
A target is a Mesh peer when it is `#` followed by at least one character
and that character is not `_`: `#_` stays reserved for the targets
§scxml-6.2.4 defines (`#_internal`, `#_parent`, `#_<invokeid>`,
`#_scxml_<sessionid>`).
The same answer is computed in several places - the C++ core's
SendHelper::isMeshTarget, the build's host_processor_analyzer::mesh_peer
(which decides at code-generation time which sends to lower to the Mesh
router), each runtime's copy (which a send site asks when a targetexpr
is evaluated, and which the Rust Mesh router reuses), and the Kotlin
router's meshPeer (which refuses a request that is not one). A target one
of them routes over Mesh and another does not would be the same document
meaning two things, so every copy reads this table.
`peer` is the name the router is addressed by, or null when the target
names no peer.
`instance` is the name the origin of an instance of an open machine,
mesh://<machine>/<instance> (docs/adr/0113, D2), is routed by on the
cores that serve an open machine (the Rust host core): the machine name
a path segment as it stands, the instance id 1 to 64 of A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ -.
A case names a peer or an instance, never both. Every other core reads
`peer` alone, and answers an instance's origin as no peer.
